active_family: 663a bounded-IV state-aware normalized-innovation conditional law; first backend is AR flow matching but backend changes require protocol diagnostics
normalization_policy: support-aware encoded levels; daily encoded increments; history-only fixed EWMA/RMS scale with robust floor; no strong rolling mean subtraction in first implementation
backend_switch_policy: Do not switch AR/one-shot, flow/diffusion/copula, or Transformer/other backbone until required audits classify the failure as backend failure rather than data framing, reconstruction, conditionality, diversity, dependency, or distribution shift.
research_axis_policy: Change one axis per iteration unless diagnostics prove coupling. Axes: data_object, temporal_factorization, backend, encoder, dependency_structure, calibration.
literature_search_policy: Search papers/official sources during diagnosis when a failure class repeats twice, a methodology/backend/encoder/temporal switch is considered, a normalization failure is not understood, local fixes are exhausted, or model limitation is about to be claimed.
current_bottleneck: 669a shows that encoded-level path scoring improves shape realism and mean reversion but does not fix level-law/distributional fidelity; it also worsens coverage. The bottleneck is now calibrated scenario width/level-law allocation, not pathwise instability or missing level awareness.
last_result_summary: 669a IV-only added level_energy_weight=0.1 to the 666a rollout objective and reached 6/11, tying 666a but not dominating it. Mean reversion passed and pathwise max-jump KS improved to 0.291, but coverage90 fell to 0.732, calibration error worsened to 0.120, level KS stayed 10/25, median-bias pass count fell to 12/25, and failed suites were coverage, conditionality, cointegration, regime coverage, and distributional fidelity.
next_step_recommendation: Keep 666a as the current clean-family baseline and keep the 669a level-energy code as a diagnostic/proper-score option. The next one-axis experiment should test a small global sampling-temperature calibration on a pathwise-strong checkpoint, because undercoverage/level-law calibration remains the main failure pattern.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. Within the clean general IV/anchor/joint state-aware normalized-innovation family, 666a is the current best: IV-only and joint38 both reach 6/11 with one sampled-rollout objective and anchor-only remains acceptable. For native IV+anchor joint generation, this is more methodologically defensible than post-hoc glued stress decks because one stochastic mechanism generates the panel.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
